reviews.reasoning: Re-derived independently against the toolkit. Ps 87 is an identity psalm (title inside MT v1, prefix_of_v1 in the device inventory), matching the row's numbering. challenges.claim: observed_substrate_signals[0] asserts oshb:Ps.87.4 and oshb:Ps.87.6 'byte-match' on the closing formula 'zeh yulad sham'; splicing both spans directly from verse_map_oshb.json shows they do not match at byte tier, only at skeleton (consonants-only) tier, four tiers below the claimed one on the campaign's own ladder (byte > nfd > accent_stripped > skeleton). This overclaim feeds directly into the row's stated confidence rationale, which leans on 'one repeated formula' as its main internal-shape evidence.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.87.4 ends ...kush zeh yulad sham (Unicode zayin+U+05B6+U+059D+U+0597, he; yod+U+05BB,lamed+U+05BC+U+05B7,dalet; shin+U+05C1+U+05B8+U+05BD,mem). oshb:Ps.87.6 ends ...amim zeh yulad sham selah (zayin+U+05B6+U+0596, he; yod+U+05BB,lamed+U+05BC+U+05B7,dalet; shin+U+05C1+U+05B8+U+05A3,mem). The zayin-word carries a different cantillation combination in each verse (U+059D+U+0597 vs U+0596), and the final mem's preceding syllable differs by exactly the disclosed hazard the toolkit itself names: v4's sham keeps meteg U+05BD (never stripped by accent_stripped), v6's sham carries the cantillation accent munach U+05A3 (stripped by accent_stripped) with no meteg. Programmatic comparison (raw ==, NFD, accent_stripped, skeleton, all via ps_lib's own normalizers) is False/False/False/True in that order: the two spans converge only at skeleton, never at byte, nfd, or accent_stripped.
